\begingroup\scriptsize
Driver statistics come from the Vulkan extension \texttt{VK\_KHR\_pipeline\_executable\_properties}. The tables describe compute kernels recorded during rendering. Scene construction and pixel packing are excluded. Register counts and spills retain the driver's native units; they must not be compared across vendors as equivalent register files. Subgroups per SIMD is a static residency limit, not measured achieved occupancy. A maximum row is the independent maximum of one metric over the rendering kernels; it does not describe a single combined kernel.\par
On Arc A380, Max live registers is ANV's peak pre-allocation register pressure. The theoretical Xe-core occupancy ceiling uses Intel's workgroup packing model with 128 hardware thread slots and 128 KiB of shared local memory per Xe-core. The calculation assumes enough workgroups and uses the compiled SIMD width, SPIR-V workgroup size and ANV's workgroup shared memory size. Actual hardware occupancy requires runtime counters.\par\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Register pressure summary}\par
Repeated runs use the maximum for each cell. A dash indicates an unavailable count.\\
\noindent 6800XT identifies AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT (RADV NAVI21) (radv Mesa 25.2.8-0ubuntu0.24.04.5, driver version 104865800, host frol-cmc, device 0)\par
\noindent A380 identifies Intel(R) Arc(tm) A380 Graphics (DG2) (Intel open-source Mesa driver Mesa 24.3.0-devel (git-9fc8668b66), driver version 100671587, host intellekt6-PC, device 0)\par
\noindent RTX4090 identifies NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA 580.178.04, driver version 2435612928, host frol-pc, device 0)\par

\noindent\textit{Fill Count}: Number of scratch fill operations.  This gives a rough estimate of the cost incurred due to spilling temporary values to memory.  If this is non-zero, you may want to adjust your shader to reduce register pressure.\par
\noindent\textit{Max live registers}: Maximum number of registers used across the entire shader.\par
\noindent\textit{Scratch Memory Size}: Number of bytes of scratch memory required by the generated shader executable.  If this is non-zero, you may want to adjust your shader to reduce register pressure.\par
\noindent\textit{Spill Count}: Number of scratch spill operations.  This gives a rough estimate of the cost incurred due to spilling temporary values to memory.  If this is non-zero, you may want to adjust your shader to reduce register pressure.\par
\noindent\textit{Theoretical Xe-core occupancy (\%)}: Modeled resident subgroups divided by 128 Xe-core hardware thread slots.\par
\noindent\textit{Theoretical resident subgroups per Xe-core}: Modeled upper bound from SIMD width, SPIR-V workgroup size and ANV shared memory, assuming enough workgroups to fill the Xe-core.\par
\noindent\textit{Workgroup Memory Size}: Number of bytes of workgroup shared memory used by this shader including any padding.\par

\noindent\textit{Scratch Memory Size}: Number of bytes of scratch memory required by the generated shader executable.  If this is non-zero, you may want to adjust your shader to reduce register pressure.\par
\noindent\textit{Spill Count}: Number of scratch spill operations.  This gives a rough estimate of the cost incurred due to spilling temporary values to memory.  If this is non-zero, you may want to adjust your shader to reduce register pressure.\par
\noindent\textit{Theoretical Xe-core occupancy (\%)}: Modeled resident subgroups divided by 128 Xe-core hardware thread slots.\par
\noindent\textit{Theoretical resident subgroups per Xe-core}: Modeled upper bound from SIMD width, SPIR-V workgroup size and ANV shared memory, assuming enough workgroups to fill the Xe-core.\par
\noindent\textit{Workgroup Memory Size}: Number of bytes of workgroup shared memory used by this shader including any padding.\par
